literal: Faren's voice was strong and large; in army camp and hunt his shouts directing ranks shook the valleys.
idiomatic: Faren's voice was huge; on campaign and hunt his commands shook the valleys.

literal: At death posthumously General Who Pacifies the East, Prince of Nan commandery, posthumous name Wei (Martial).
idiomatic: At death posthumously General Who Pacifies the East, Prince of Nan, posthumous name Martial.

literal: Zhu Xiuzhi had served Song as consulting staff officer to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi had served Song as consulting staff officer to the Minister of Works.

literal: He held Huatai and was captured by An Ji.
idiomatic: He held Huatai and was taken by An Ji.

literal: Taiwu praised his firm defense, gave him an imperial-clan woman in marriage, made him Regional Commander of Yunzhong.
idiomatic: Taiwu praised his defense, married him an imperial-clan woman, made him Regional Commander of Yunzhong.

literal: Later he fled to Feng Hong.
idiomatic: Later he fled to Feng Hong.

literal: Hong sent him to the south.
idiomatic: Hong sent him to the south.

literal: When Ji took Huatai, Song's Administrator of Chenliu Yan Ling garrisoned Cangyuan.
idiomatic: When Ji took Huatai, Song's Chenliu Administrator Yan Ling held Cangyuan.

literal: When Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin's army reached Yingchuan, Ling led five hundred civil and military men to Jin to surrender.
idiomatic: When Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin reached Yingchuan, Ling led five hundred officials and soldiers to surrender.

literal: Mingyuan praised his sincere submission, enfeoffed Marquis of Heyang, acting Governor of Jingzhou.
idiomatic: Mingyuan praised his sincerity, enfeoffed Marquis of Heyang, acting Governor of Jingzhou.

literal: He followed the imperial campaign south, returned as honored guest.
idiomatic: He followed the southern campaign and returned as honored guest.

literal: When Taiwu ascended, for merit in submission he was made Administrator of Zhongshan, famed for pure conduct.
idiomatic: When Taiwu took the throne, for submitting he was made Administrator of Zhongshan, famed for purity.

literal: He died at home.
idiomatic: He died at home.

literal: Son Youyu inherited.
idiomatic: Son Youyu inherited.

literal: Ling once had a separate biography; now it is appended here.
idiomatic: Ling once had his own biography; it is appended here.

literal: Xiuzhi was eminent in Song; the affairs are fully in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi was eminent in Song; the full account is in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

literal: Tang He, styled Youqi, native of Xiyi'an in Jin.
idiomatic: Tang He, styled Youqi, of Xiyi'an in Jin.

literal: Father Yao, because Liang lands were in turmoil, installed Liang Wuzhao Wang Ba in the lands west of the river.
idiomatic: His father Yao, when Liang was in chaos, set up Wuzhao Wang Ba west of the river.

literal: When Liang fell, He and elder brother Qi took their nephew, Wuzhao Wang's grandson Bao, and fled to Yiwu.
idiomatic: When Liang fell He and brother Qi took nephew Bao, Wuzhao's grandson, and fled to Yiwu.

literal: He gathered more than two thousand households and submitted to the Rouran.
idiomatic: He gathered more than two thousand households and submitted to the Rouran.

literal: The Rouran made Qi King of Yiwu.
idiomatic: The Rouran made Qi King of Yiwu.

literal: After twenty years He and Qi sent envoys to surrender to Wei but were pressed by the Rouran and therefore led their tribes to Gaochang.
idiomatic: After twenty years they sent envoys to Wei; the Rouran pressed them and they led their people to Gaochang.

literal: The Rouran sent a tribal chief A Ruo to attack He, reaching Baili City.
idiomatic: The Rouran sent chief A Ruo against He to Baili City.

literal: He first attacked Gaoning.
idiomatic: He first attacked Gaoning.

literal: Qi fought A Ruo and fell; He gathered the remainder and fled to the Former Kingdom.
idiomatic: Qi fought A Ruo and died; He gathered the rest and fled to the Former Kingdom.

literal: At the time Juqu Anzhou held Hengjie City; He attacked and took it.
idiomatic: Juqu Anzhou held Hengjie City; He took it.

literal: He beheaded Anzhou's nephew Shu, also took Gaoning and Baili cities.
idiomatic: He beheaded Anzhou's nephew Shu and took Gaoning and Baili.

literal: He sent a memorial reporting.
idiomatic: He sent a memorial reporting.

literal: Taiwu praised him and repeatedly granted sealed edicts.
idiomatic: Taiwu praised him and repeatedly sent sealed edicts.

literal: Later He and the Former Kingdom's king Che Yiluo destroyed Anzhou.
idiomatic: Later He and Former Kingdom king Che Yiluo destroyed Anzhou.

literal: Taiwu sent Duke of Zhou Wan Dugui to campaign against Yanqi; edict had He and Yiluo lead their followers to Dugui and persuade the six cities east of Liulü.
idiomatic: Taiwu sent Wan Dugui against Yanqi; He and Yiluo were to join him and win the six cities east of Liulü.

literal: Together they attacked Bojuluo City and took it.
idiomatic: Together they attacked Bojuluo City and took it.

literal: Later on joint campaign against Kucha, Dugui ordered He to garrison Yanqi.
idiomatic: On joint campaign against Kucha Dugui left He to hold Yanqi.

literal: At the time the garrison chief of Liulü, Yizhenjia, was about to rebel; He went straight into his city and seized and beheaded Yizhenjia.
idiomatic: Liulü garrison chief Yizhenjia was about to rebel; He entered his city and beheaded him.

literal: By this the Western Regions were pacified; He had strength in it.
idiomatic: The Western Regions were pacified; He had a hand in it.

literal: Son Qin, styled Mengzhen, post of Governor of Shanzhou.
idiomatic: Son Qin, styled Mengzhen, was Governor of Shanzhou.

literal: Reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: His title was reduced to marquis.

literal: At death son Jingxuan inherited.
idiomatic: At death son Jingxuan inherited.

literal: Died as Administrator of the Eastern Capital.
idiomatic: He died as Administrator of the Eastern Capital.

literal: Qi's son Xuanda, nature resolute and bold, had his father's manner.
idiomatic: Qi's son Xuanda was resolute and bold like his father.

literal: With uncle He he came to court and both were honored guests, enfeoffed Duke of Jinchang.
idiomatic: With uncle He he came to court; both were honored guests, enfeoffed Duke of Jinchang.

literal: In Xianwen's time post of Governor of Huazhou.
idiomatic: In Xianwen's time he was Governor of Huazhou.

literal: In Taihe year 16 reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: In Taihe 16 he was reduced to marquis.

literal: Son Chong, styled Jizu, inherited.
idiomatic: Son Chong, styled Jizu, inherited.

literal: Kou Zan, styled Fengguo, native of Shanggu, because of hardship moved to Wan'nian in Fengyi.
idiomatic: Kou Zan, styled Fengguo, of Shanggu, moved to Wan'nian in Fengyi in hardship.

literal: Father Xiuzhi, styled Yanqi, Administrator of Donglai under Fu Jian.
idiomatic: Father Xiuzhi, styled Yanqi, was Donglai Administrator under Fu Jian.

literal: Zan's younger brother Qian had the Way; Taiwu greatly respected him, therefore posthumously made Xiuzhi General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qinzhou, Duke of Fengyi.
idiomatic: Brother Qian had the Way; Taiwu respected him and posthumously made Xiuzhi General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qin, Duke of Fengyi.

literal: Granted funeral robes, posthumous name Duke Ai.
idiomatic: Funeral robes were granted, posthumous Duke Ai.

literal: Edict had Qin and Yong provinces erect stele and tomb.
idiomatic: An edict had Qin and Yong erect stele and tomb.

literal: Also posthumously made Xi's mother Lady of Fengyi, and sixteen clansmen posthumously administrators, magistrates, marquises, viscounts, barons — seven commanderies and five counties in active office.
idiomatic: Xi's mother was made Lady of Fengyi; sixteen kin were posthumously administrators, magistrates, and nobles—seven commanderies, five counties in office.

literal: Zan from youth was famed for purity.
idiomatic: Zan was famed young for purity.

literal: Eight feet tall, bearing stern and lofty, he did not move outside ritual.
idiomatic: Eight feet tall, stern bearing—he would not stir outside ritual.

literal: Fu Jian's Vice Director Wei Hua, a lofty man of the province, though years differed always treated him with shared taste.
idiomatic: Fu Jian's Vice Director Wei Hua, a provincial worthy, though older always treated him as an equal in taste.

literal: When Hua was Administrator of Fengyi he summoned Zan as merit officer.
idiomatic: When Hua was Fengyi Administrator he summoned Zan as merit officer.

literal: Later made magistrate of Xiangyi.
idiomatic: Later he was made magistrate of Xiangyi.

literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed more than a thousand families of Qin and Yong made Zan their leader and came to Wei.
idiomatic: When Yao Hong fell more than a thousand Qin and Yong families made Zan leader and came to Wei.

literal: Made Administrator of Henan commandery.
idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Henan.

literal: Afterward Qin and Yong men who fled to Henan, Xingyang, and Henei reached ten thousand households; Zan was made Governor of Southern Yong, Marquis of Zhiji, and Yong province commanderies and counties were set up at Luoyang to settle them.
idiomatic: Later ten thousand Qin and Yong households fled to Henan, Xingyang, and Henei; Zan was Southern Yong Governor, Marquis of Zhiji, with Yong counties at Luoyang to settle them.

literal: Thus refugees came on backs and in slings from afar, more than double before.
idiomatic: Refugees came on backs and in slings from afar, more than double before.

literal: Zan's rank advanced to Duke of Henan, added General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel of the Southern Man, still governor.
idiomatic: He rose to Duke of Henan, General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel of the Southern Man, still governor.

literal: Luoyang and Yuzhou refugee commanderies were added to his charge.
idiomatic: Luoyang and Yuzhou refugee commanderies were added.

literal: Though rank and title were heavy he never tired in receiving people.
idiomatic: Though rank was heavy he never tired of receiving people.

literal: Earlier before Zan was noble he once had physiognomist Tang Wen read him.
idiomatic: Before he was noble Zan had physiognomist Tang Wen read him.

literal: Wen said: "The black mole on your brow enters the cap — rank will reach regional lord, enfeoffed duke."
idiomatic: Wen said, "The black mole on your brow enters the cap—you will reach regional lord, be enfeoffed duke."

literal: When he was noble Wen came in commoner's rites and bowed: "My lord, do you recall what I said before?"
idiomatic: When he was noble Wen bowed as a commoner: "My lord, do you recall my words?"

literal: Yanwen sat and said: "In the past you said Du Qiong could not be a chief official; all thought otherwise.
idiomatic: Yanwen sat and said, "You once said Du Qiong could not be chief official; all disagreed.

literal: When Qiong became magistrate of Zhouzhi you still said the physiognomy did not show it, yet Qiong indeed died suddenly of violent illness before taking office."
idiomatic: When Qiong became Zhouzhi magistrate you said the face did not show it—yet Qiong died suddenly before taking office."

literal: In old times Wei Shu saw his master's son die and knew he himself would reach duke.
idiomatic: Wei Shu once saw his master's son die and knew he would reach duke.

literal: I always took your judgment of Qiong as proof and never ceased this hope."
idiomatic: I always took your judgment of Qiong as proof and never lost hope."

literal: He therefore granted Wen robes and a fine horse.
idiomatic: He granted Wen robes and a fine horse.

literal: Zan seventeen years in the province greatly won public and private praise.
idiomatic: Seventeen years in the province he won public and private praise.

literal: Old, he asked to retire.
idiomatic: In old age he asked to retire.

literal: At death he ordered a thin burial in timely dress.
idiomatic: At death he ordered thin burial in timely dress.

literal: Taiwu mourned him, posthumous name Duke Xuanmu.
idiomatic: Taiwu mourned him, posthumous Duke Xuanmu.

literal: Son Yuanbao inherited.
idiomatic: Son Yuanbao inherited.

literal: Yuanbao's younger brother Zhen, styled Xiansheng.
idiomatic: Younger brother Zhen, styled Xiansheng.

literal: At twelve he met father's death; in mourning famed for filial piety.
idiomatic: At twelve he met his father's death; mourning made him famed for filial piety.

literal: Light with wealth, fond of scholars.
idiomatic: He was light with wealth and fond of scholars.

literal: At the end of Xianwen he was Administrator of Zhongchuan.
idiomatic: At the end of Xianwen he was Administrator of Zhongchuan.

literal: At the time Feng Xi was Governor of Luozhou, government marked by greed and cruelty; Xiansheng slightly attached to him and greatly won his favor.
idiomatic: Feng Xi was Luozhou Governor, greedy and cruel; Xiansheng attached to him slightly and won his favor.

literal: Later Administrator of Hongnong.
idiomatic: Later Administrator of Hongnong.

literal: Convicted of taking bribes, impeached by the censor, dismissed, died at home.
idiomatic: Convicted of bribes, impeached by the censor, dismissed, died at home.

literal: Son Zuxun, Administrator of Shunyang.
idiomatic: Son Zuxun, Administrator of Shunyang.

literal: Zuxun's younger brother Zuli.
idiomatic: Zuxun's younger brother Zuli.

literal: The brothers were all filial, friendly, and grave; white-haired they dwelt together.
idiomatic: The brothers were filial, friendly, and grave; white-haired they lived together.

literal: Though parents had long died, in the hall where they had lived in life they still set curtains, folding stools, and staffs, and at seasons opened the hall and bowed in rows;
idiomatic: Though parents were long dead, in their old hall they still set curtains, stools, and staffs; at seasons they opened the hall and bowed in rows;

literal: weeping they offered sacrifice as at the ancestral temple.
idiomatic: weeping they offered sacrifice as at a temple.

literal: For auspicious or inauspicious matters they always reported first; returning from a distant journey was the same.
idiomatic: For good or ill they always reported first; returning from travel was the same.

literal: Zuli at the end of Emperor Xuanwu was Governor of Hezhou.
idiomatic: Zuli at the end of Xuanwu was Governor of Hezhou.

literal: Several years in office he met Xi Tiejiong's sudden rebellion; also city men went to the capital to list sixteen articles of his greed.
idiomatic: In office he met Xi Tiejiong's rebellion; city men also listed sixteen charges of greed at court.

literal: He was spared by amnesty.
idiomatic: Amnesty spared him.

literal: After long time concurrently Commandant of the Court, also concurrently Vice Director of Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Long after he was concurrently Court Commandant and Vice Director of Masters of Writing.

literal: He feared powerful houses, accommodated their faces and colors, and could not hold to principle.
idiomatic: He feared powerful houses, accommodated their moods, and could not hold principle.

literal: Later when barbarians rebelled at Sanya he was commander pursuing them and died in battle.
idiomatic: Later barbarians rebelled at Sanya; as commander he pursued them and died in battle.

literal: Posthumously Defender-General, Director of Seven Armies, Governor of Yongzhou, Baron of Changping.
idiomatic: Posthumously Defender-General, Director of Seven Armies, Governor of Yong, Baron of Changping.

literal: Zuli's younger brother Jun.
idiomatic: Zuli's younger brother Jun.

literal: Jun styled Zujun.
idiomatic: Jun was styled Zujun.

literal: By nature broad and elegant, from youth had judgment, loved learning and strong memory.
idiomatic: Broad and elegant by nature, from youth he had judgment, loved learning, remembered well.

literal: By nature also lenient and forgiving, he did not set his heart on wealth.
idiomatic: He was also lenient and forgiving and did not set his heart on wealth.

literal: The household once sold goods to someone and wrongly gained one bolt of silk.
idiomatic: The household once sold goods and wrongly gained one bolt of silk.
